1006: Each region of Thailand has its own dialect.
Thai food varies more by season than by region.
Every province has a dish it's known for.
1007: Northern food is much milder than the rest.
Southern food is known for its coconut curries.
Isan food is famed as the spiciest in Thailand.
1008: Northerners eat plain rice, unlike Isan folk.
Isan folk eat sticky rice with almost everything.
Sticky rice is eaten mostly in the north-east.
1009: Som tam and laab are best eaten with sticky rice.
Som tam is the one Isan dish everyone knows.
Isan food has become popular abroad as well.
1010: Travelling abroad, Thais look for Thai restaurants.
Travelling upcountry, Thais stop at markets along the way.
Every province has a dish worth going out of your way for.
1011: Every trip back, you always bring something for the office.
You're expected to bring something back for everyone.
Most people buy their souvenirs at the airport.
1012: Thais think eating alone is a bit sad.
Thais will often eat together before talking business.
Sharing food is how friendships get made here.
1013: Inviting people to your home is very normal here.
Refusing an invitation to eat can seem rude.
Paying for the meal is how you show respect.
1014: A host should always eat last.
Guests are expected to bring something with them.
A good host never lets a glass go empty.
1015: If you're full, just leave a little on the plate.
It's rude to finish everything you're given.
You should wait to be offered before taking more.
1016: When Thais ask where you're going, they aren't asking literally.
If someone asks whether you've eaten, they may be about to feed you.
'Have you eaten?' is the first thing people ask here.
1017: The saying about one chilli-dip bowl is about sharing what little you have.
There's a saying that a couple should eat from the same plate.
Old sayings about food usually turn out to be about family.
1018: Thais use chopsticks for noodles, not for rice.
The fork is only used to push food onto the spoon.
Thais eat sticky rice with their hands, not with cutlery.
1019: Children are taught to finish everything on their plate.
Elders always say you should eat while it's hot.
Wasting food is said to bring bad luck.
1020: A Thai meal is usually served all at once, rather than in courses.
Soup is often served on the side, as part of a Thai meal.
Each person gets their own plate of rice, and the dishes are shared.
1021: Mum goes to the supermarket about once a week.
Mum likes going to the market early before it gets hot.
Mum buys fruit at the market on her way home.
1022: These days people choose a restaurant based on the photos rather than the food itself.
Restaurants now design their dishes to look good online more than to taste good.
Many people won't start eating until everyone at the table has taken a photo.
1023: At temple events everyone brings a dish to share.
There's always far too much food at these things.
The monks eat first at a merit-making event.
1024: Thais would rather take leftovers home — better than ordering too little.
Running out in front of guests is embarrassing — so people over-cater.
Ordering too much is seen as wasteful — people are more careful now.
1025: Thai restaurants have opened in almost every country — there's one in most towns now.
Most people get to know Thailand through its food — it's often their first taste of it.
Thai food abroad is adapted to local tastes — which is why it barely tastes Thai now.
1026: The stalls by the road sell drinks and snacks, mostly.
You'll find a market in every town along the way.
Roadside stalls are cheap, far cheaper than any restaurant.
1027: Japanese food has become especially popular here, more than any other foreign food.
Young people would rather eat foreign food than Thai food these days.
Thai food abroad is nothing like the real thing, whatever the menu says.
2256: Thailand's known for being cheap to travel in — that's why people come back.
People here stay friendly — even when they're rushed off their feet.
Service has got worse in the tourist areas — you notice it straight away.

1006.q: Each region of Thailand has food with its own identity.
1006.nat: Each region of Thailand has its own distinctive food.

1007.q: Food of the South is renowned as the spiciest in Thailand.
1007.nat: Southern food is famed as the spiciest in Thailand.

1009.q: Som tam and laab are Isan food that people all over the country love.
1009.nat: Som tam and laab are Isan dishes the whole country's hooked on.

1010.q: When Thais go upcountry, they like to seek out the food that place is famous for.
1010.nat: Travelling upcountry, Thais seek out the local specialty.

1011.q: Whenever you return from upcountry, you must always buy something to bring back as a food gift.
1011.nat: Every trip back, you always bring food gifts home.

1012.q: Thais see the act of eating together as something that helps bond relationships.
1012.nat: Thais see eating together as relationship-building.

1014.q: Hosts tend to feed their guests well, and always with good food.
1014.nat: A host always feeds their guests generously.

1015.q: Even if you are full already, if the host invites you to eat more, then you shouldn't refuse.
1015.nat: Even if you're full, you shouldn't refuse the host's offer.

1016.q: When Thais ask whether you've eaten yet, sometimes it's just a greeting, nothing more.
1016.nat: When Thais ask 'have you eaten?', sometimes it's just a greeting.

1017.q: Thais have an idiom that to eat from a single bowl of chilli dip means being faithful.
1017.nat: The idiom 'eating from one chili-dip bowl' means being faithful to one partner.

1019.q: Elders often teach you: don't eat your rice and leave some to be thrown away.
1019.nat: Elders teach you not to waste rice.

1022.q: Nowadays many go to restaurants to take photos to post on social media more than to actually eat.
1022.nat: These days many go to restaurants to photograph food for social media more than to actually eat.

1023.q: Whenever there's a merit-making event, there's always food laid on to feed loads of people.
1023.nat: Merit-making events always lay on lots of food for everyone.

1024.q: Thais like to order lots extra to spare — leftovers are still better than running short.
1024.nat: Thais like to over-order — better to have extra than run short.

2256.q: Thailand is famous for service with a smile — whichever place you go to, you'll find it.
2256.nat: Thailand's known for service with a smile — you see it wherever you go.
